subject: Demo request — high throughput use case
content:
From: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request — high throughput use case

Hi Evelyn,

We signed up for the self-serve tier yesterday and I'd love to schedule a quick walkthrough of Redwood for a potential POC. High level: we’re an e-commerce platform (FastRetail) with periodic marketing campaigns that spike request volume. Primary goals are throughput, predictable latency during campaigns, and cost controls.

A couple quick pieces of context:
- Avg monthly tokens today: ~50M (expected to grow if POC goes well)
- Peak concurrency during promos: approx 150-250 qps for short windows
- Security: SSO (Okta) required for pilots; we may need DLP questions later

I attached a small traffic snapshot (traffic_profile_Q1.csv) with recent hourly peaks to help scope. Can you propose 30-min slots this week? Please include our infra lead, Lara (cc'd here).

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of ML Ops, FastRetail
[samir@fastretail.io]

Attachment: traffic_profile_Q1.csv (CSV, 34KB)

----
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara@fastretail.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo request — high throughput use case

Hi Samir 9

Thanks for the context and the traffic snapshot99this is helpful. Before we lock a slot I'd like to confirm a few quick items so we tailor the demo:

1) Primary use-case: is the demo focused on generation for UX (assistant/chat) or backend batch inference/embeddings for search/rerank?
2) Typical request size (tokens) and avg sequence length for the high-volume flows?
3) Do you need guaranteed throughput SLA for the POC, or are you flexible with best-effort and guidance on scaling?
4) Any compliance requirements (data residency, SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM)?
5) Preferred region (us/eu/apac) for the demo environment.

For slots I have open (PT):
- Fri, 17 Mar 2028 — 10:00am (30m)
- Mon, 20 Mar 2028 — 9:00am (30m)

If either works, I can send a calendar invite and loop in Monica from Solutions to cover throughput/architecture. If helpful, here's a short calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo-30

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com

----
On Thu, Mar 15, 2028 at 08:20 AM, Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io> wrote:
From: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara@fastretail.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:20:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo request — high throughput use case

Thanks, Evelyn. Answers inline: 

1) Primary use-case: mixture. Main consumer-facing flows are generation (assistant responses, short prompts ~60-120 tokens). We also run nightly embedding jobs for search re-ranking (longer sequences occasionally).
2) Typical request size: 80-150 tokens; nightly batches up to 2k tokens per job.
3) For POC we need predictable performance but a hard SLA isn't required yet; we’d like guidance on Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable throughput.
4) Compliance: SOC2 is relevant; we will ask security questions later. KMS for keying is a plus but not blocking.
5) Region: primary users in US.

Timeline: hoping to kick off a POC in ~6 weeks.
Traffic: monthly token baseline ~50M; ramp scenarios during promos could push to ~200 qps sustained for short bursts (1-4 hours).

I've attached a slightly more detailed workbook (fastretail_campaigns.xlsx) with campaign patterns and an internal note about burst windows.

Can we lock Fri 17 Mar 10:00am PT? Lara (cc) will join and may want to ask about deployment options.

- Samir

Attachments: fastretail_campaigns.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Monica,

Forwarding Samir's note and the campaign workbook. They’re targeting a POC in ~6 weeks, baseline ~50M tokens/month with promo bursts up to ~200 qps for a few hours. Primary wants: predictable latency under burst, cost controls, and SSO. Region: US.

Can you lead the demo on Fri 17 Mar 10:00am PT? If yes, please cover:
- Throughput architecture (batching, KV cache, autoscaling profiles)
- Fallbacks / model-variant routing for graceful degradation
- Quantization / cost tradeoffs at a high level
- Notes we should surface for their security contacts (SOC2, KMS)

I added a short prep doc (demo_prep_notes.pdf) with suggested slides.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Hi all,

I can take the demo on Fri, 17 Mar at 10:00am PT. I'll focus the 30 minutes on:
- How Redwood manages bursty qps: continuous batching, smart scheduling, and autoscale buffers
- KV/prefix caching to reduce per-token work for assistant flows
- Model routing and fallback behavior (how we fail down to smaller variants gracefully)
- Quick estimation of cost tradeoffs (quantized endpoints vs full precision)

Evelyn, I'll use the prep doc and slot in a brief architecture diagram + one slide with recommended Dedicated vs Hosted options for a 6-week POC. Samir/Lara: I'll also add a short appendix slide with the SOC2/KMS checklist so you have items to share with security.

I've created the HubSpot meeting record (HS-10234) and will send a calendar invite from calendly via the team.

See you Friday.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
